title: Two-week KPI cadence and experiment log
content:
Context:
This is a personal two-week cadence note for tracking small, measurable improvements tied to my role (developer experience) — shipping docs/templates, reducing PR cycle time, and targeted mentoring.

Sprint window: 2026-02-17 -> 2026-03-01 (two-week box)
Purpose: keep things compact, run 2 micro-experiments per sprint, and have an explicit success metric for each.

Top-level goals (owner = me):
- Goal A (productivity): Reduce average PR review turnaround for core SDK repo to <24h for non-blocking PRs.
  - Why: faster iteration, fewer blocked tasks for other teams.
  - Baseline: 36h (last 2 weeks)
  - Success target for this sprint: 20h median
  - Action plan: 1) dedicated "review hour" every weekday 10:30-11:30; 2) create a short PR checklist template for common review feedback; 3) mark 'review-friendly' label on small PRs.

- Goal B (impact / reach): Ship 2 concise how-to templates for onboarding new internal infra contractors (runtime deploy + debug checklist).
  - Baseline: zero consolidated templates; onboarding friction reported in #infra-handoff
  - Success target: 2 templates published in devex repo + 1 quick walkthrough session recorded (~15m).
  - Action plan: draft templates Mon-Wed; pair with Infra Eng on Thurs; record Fri.

- Goal C (people / mentorship): Run 1 paired debugging session with a junior engineer and log outcomes.
  - Success target: junior can onboard and run local inference end-to-end without my help on second attempt.

Micro-experiments (this sprint):
- Experiment 1: "Review-hour" block effectiveness
  - Hypothesis: if I block 1 hour each weekday for reviews, median PR turnaround will drop by >=30%.
  - Measurement: track PRs reviewed by me during 10:30-11:30 and compute median time-to-merge vs baseline.
  - Success criteria: median <= 25h and at least 6 small PRs merged this sprint.
  - Notes to self: be strict about not multitasking during the hour; set Do-Not-Disturb on Slack.

- Experiment 2: "Tiny-template" onboarding
  - Hypothesis: having 2 one-page templates will reduce onboarding questions by >40% in first week after publish (tracked via #infra-handoff mentions and a quick Google Form link in the README).
  - Measurement: count direct questions referencing steps the templates cover vs previous two weeks.
  - Success criteria: drop in repeated questions and at least 1 positive comment on templates in Slack.

Weekly check-in snapshots:
- Week 1 (Mon-Wed):
  - Progress: drafted first template for runtime deploy; created PR checklist draft; scheduled walkthrough with Jose from Infra for Thu; review-hour started Monday.
  - Metrics observed: PRs I touched during review-hour were merged faster, anecdotal only (need to compute numbers later).
  - Blockers: had two unplanned incident follow-ups (took 3 hrs total) that pushed template work later.
  - Note: incident work valuable but noisy; need to preserve at least 3 review-hour slots per week.

- Week 2 (Thu-Fri):
  - Progress: walked templates with Jose, edits done; recorded 14m walkthrough with screen capture; published templates to devex/docs; added quick feedback form link.
  - Metrics observed: PR checklist reduced one round of style feedback in a small PR.
  - Pairing: paired debugging with Priya on Friday; she reproduced local issue, applied fix, needed one follow-up review.

Quantitative log (for end-of-sprint analysis):
- PR review median start->merge (baseline 36h): current sprint median (preliminary) 22h (need to verify via GH API).
- PRs merged that I reviewed during 10:30-11:30: 7
- Templates published: 2 (runtime-deploy.md, debug-checklist.md)
- Views on walkthrough video: 12 in first 48h
- Onboarding questions referencing solved steps: down from ~11 -> 5 (quick Slack search)

Retrospective (quick):
- What worked:
  - Review-hour produced tangible speedups for small PRs.
  - Templates forced me to think about explicit assumptions new hires miss.
  - Pair session accelerated junior onboarding.
- What didn't:
  - Incidents ate into deep work; need better escalation to avoid losing templating momentum.
  - Measurement gaps: I didn't hook up the GH API at the start; manual search is a pain.

Decisions and next actions (owner tags in parens):
- Keep the review-hour habit for next sprint, but move it to 10:00-11:00 to match timezone overlap (Oliver).
- Add a tiny GH Actions job to tag review-hour PRs automatically (low effort) and compute median times (Oliver + DevOps).
- Triage process: suggest a "soft-hold" policy for non-sev incidents during template publishing windows; discuss with SRE (Oliver to draft RFC).
- Iterate templates into a "1-pager checklist" canonical location and add to new-hire checklist (Oliver + Maya).

Open questions / risks:
- Will teams adopt the 'review-friendly' label or ignore it? Plan: demo in weekly eng-all.
- If incidents keep eating time, behavior will regress. Consider protected focus days.

Notes to self:
- Keep experiment small and measurable; avoid turning templates into big docs.
- Automate measurement early next sprint (save manual time).
- Capture one short quote from Priya about the pair session to add to template README.

Quick links (for follow-up):
- PR checklist draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/blob/main/pr-checklist.md
- Templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/tree/main/onboarding-templates
- Walkthrough recording: internal drive link (will upload under devex/playbooks)

End of sprint note: preliminary pass suggests both experiments had positive signal. Next sprint focus: automate measurement, keep 2 experiments but one focused on long-term adoption (labels + walkthrough), and one on sustaining review cadence.

-- Oliver
